blocks.text: From Lesson 1 you own palvelu and the adjective-slot trick. But reviews almost never stop at 'good service' — they immediately move on to the two things Finns really judge a repair shop on: the place itself (korjaamo) and the price (hinta). This lesson gives you both words, plus your first real taste of Finnish past tense: oli.

blocks.title: Why price gets its own sentence
blocks.text: In these reviews, praise for service and judgement on price are almost always kept separate — a shop can get 'ystävällinen palvelu' and still lose a star over hinta. Finns tend to state the verdict on price bluntly and briefly, then move on. There's rarely hedging: it's either kohtuullinen (reasonable) or kallis (expensive), and reviewers say so directly.

blocks.content: {Korjaamo|word|noun|repair shop} means 'repair shop' or 'garage'. It comes from korjata, 'to fix/repair'. You'll also see {huolto|word|noun|service/maintenance} (maintenance) and the compound {autohuolto|word|compound noun|car service centre} — literally auto (car) + huolto (service), stuck together. Finnish loves building long words this way instead of using extra prepositions.

items.en: I don't recommend this repair shop.

items.fi: Vein autoni {autohuoltoon|grammar|illative|to the car service centre}.
items.en: I took my car to the car service centre.

blocks.title: Compound words — free vocabulary
blocks.text: Once you know auto (car) and huolto (service), you already understand autohuolto without learning a new word. Finnish builds enormous vocabulary this way: two known words glued together make a third. Watch for this pattern constantly — it will save you far more effort than it costs.
Piece 2 — Hinta: price and its verdicts

blocks.content: {Hinta|word|noun|price} is 'price'. Its most common companion word is {hinta-arvio|phrase|compound noun|price estimate} — hinta (price) + arvio (estimate). Reviewers love saying whether the hinta-arvio piti paikkansa — 'held its place', meaning the estimate turned out to be accurate.

blocks.title: On becomes oli — your first past tense
blocks.text: You already know on means 'is'. Its past tense is simply {oli|grammar|past tense of 'on'|was} — 'was'. That's the whole rule for this verb: on → oli. No new endings, no exceptions. Palvelu on hyvä (the service is good) becomes Palvelu oli hyvä (the service was good) — just swap on for oli.

blocks.title: A verb with no 'I' or 'you'
blocks.text: {Kannattaa|grammar|impersonal verb|it's worth (doing)} doesn't take a personal subject like suosittelen does. It just sits there meaning 'it's worth it / it pays to'. Reviewers use it to give advice: Kannattaa pyytää tarjous kirjallisena — 'It's worth asking for a quote in writing.' Think of it like English 'worth it' — no one says 'I worth it', it just floats free.

items.fi: {Kannattaa|grammar|impersonal verb|it's worth it} pyytää tarjous kirjallisena.
items.en: It's worth asking for a quote in writing.

items.fi: {Kannattaa|grammar|impersonal verb|it's worth it} kiinnittää huomiota hintaan.
items.en: It's worth paying attention to the price.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: What was the price like at the repair shop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Hinta oli kohtuullinen, ja hinta-arvio piti paikkansa.
lines.en: The price was reasonable, and the estimate was accurate.

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Palvelu oli hyvä. Kannattaa käydä siellä.
lines.en: The service was good. It's worth going there.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: You now have two ways to end a positive review: suosittelen (I recommend — personal, Lesson 1) and kannattaa (it's worth it — impersonal, this lesson). Native reviewers switch between them freely. You can too, once you feel which one fits: is it your opinion (suosittelen), or general advice (kannattaa)?

blocks.content: Korjaamo: KOR-yaa-mo (the 'j' is like English 'y', and the double 'aa' is a long, held vowel — not two separate a's). Hinta: HIN-ta (short, crisp, stress on HIN). Kannattaa: KAN-nat-taa (double consonants n and t are held slightly longer than single ones — this changes meaning in Finnish, so don't rush them).

blocks.title: What you now own
items: korjaamo — repair shop, and huolto — service (which combine into autohuolto)
on → oli — your first past tense pattern, no exceptions
piti paikkansa — held true, was accurate
kannattaa — it's worth it (an impersonal verb with no 'I')
You can now judge and describe both the shop and its price, in the past tense
You can build new compound words yourself just by knowing their parts
